- New-onset persistent fatigue  
- Mild normocytic/normochromic anemia (Hb = 10 g/dL)  
- Absence of fever, night sweats, or lymphadenopathy

- No gastrointestinal symptoms reported — but GI malignancies (especially right-sided colon cancer) frequently present *without* overt GI complaints (e.g., bleeding may be occult, diarrhea/constipation absent)  

[GAPS]  
- Patient’s age — critical for malignancy risk stratification and screening recommendations (e.g., colonoscopy indicated at ≥45 years)  
- Stool testing: FIT or fecal occult blood test (FOBT) — not yet performed, though explicitly noted as pending  
- Serum ferritin — needed to determine if anemia is iron-deficient (suggestive of chronic GI blood loss)  
- Colonoscopy or other GI imaging results — not yet obtained  
- Peripheral blood smear review — not performed, so dysplasia or abnormal cells cannot be ruled out  
- Age-appropriate cancer screening status (e.g., prior colonoscopy, family history details) — not specified  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Colorectal adenocarcinoma
